title: Find the Number of Good Pairs I
summary: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of lengths n and m, and a positive integer k, count the pairs (i, j) where nums1[i] is divisible by nums2[j] multiplied by k.
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of lengths n and m, and a positive integer k, count the pairs (i, j) where nums1[i] is divisible by nums2[j] multiplied by k.
constraints: An index pair i,j is good when nums1[i] is divisible by nums2[j]*k.
Count pairs by index, so repeated values create separate pairs.
Return the number of good pairs.
reference_solution:
def count_scaled_divisible_pairs(nums1,nums2,k):
    return sum(a%(b*k)==0 for a in nums1 for b in nums2)
hints: The source-I constraints permit checking each Cartesian-product pair.
For a,b test whether the remainder modulo b*k is zero.
Add the Boolean result for every index combination.
The nested iteration visits each index pair once, preserving multiplicity exactly.
